answer: An agent economy can resist sybil attacks with a stake-weighted reputation graph. Each agent is a vertex whose standing grows only from verified work and locked collateral. New identities start at the mesa of zero trust, where every action is visible yet costly to fake, since each vertex must post a bond before transacting. Reputation never travels by whisper: unverified claims carry no weight, and endorsements decay without real work. An attacker spinning up thousands of fake agents must pay its own stake for every vertex, so the cost of a fake army exceeds any profit from gaming the system.
